title: This Week's Weird News 10/30/26 | KFYR 550 AM / 99.7 FM
site_name: Coast to Coast AM with George Noory
excerpt: A pair of possible cryptid sightings in South America, a pill-shaped UFO spotted by the crew of an aircraft flying over Ohio, and an alleged catnapping case in Texas were among the weird and wondrous stories to cross our desk this past week.
content:
A pair of possible cryptid sightings in South America, a pill-shaped UFO spotted by the crew of an aircraft flying over Ohio, and an alleged catnapping case in Texas were among the weird and wondrous stories to cross our desk this past week.

A pair of peculiar UFO sightings caught our attention this past week. First, in Oregon, a spellbound witness captured footage of several inordinately bright orbs that were observed hovering over the city of Portland for around 30 minutes. Shortly after disappearing, another pair of puzzling lights appeared and remained in place for a half-hour before also vanishing. Among the theories put forward for the illuminations were normal air traffic, which seems unlikely given how they remained stationary for so long, drones, and, of course, aliens. Later in the week, it was revealed that the flight crew of a private aircraft cruising over Ohio spotted a silvery pill-shaped object that hovered outside their plane, but did not appear on their radar or that of the nearest air traffic control tower.

While Bigfoot and the Loch Ness Monster may garner the lion's share of headlines when it comes to cryptids, there are a vast array of legendary creatures said to exist around the world. This past week saw two such legendary animals pop up in the news. In Chile, a group of astonished fishermen captured footage of an encounter with an unknown aquatic animal with a strange circular shape. The baffling creature immediately drew comparisons to a regional folkloric 'water spirit' known as El Cuero, which is said to boast a flattened body that it uses to envelop its prey. Meanwhile, in Argentina, a group of friends filmed a diminutive, hair-covered figure that some suggested was a similarly apocryphal goblin-like cryptid dubbed the Pombero.

By far the weirdest story of the week came from Texas, where a family accused their neighbor of taking their cat and leaving it nearly 100 miles away from where they live. The case began when Alyssa and Patrick Duffy's pet Tabby, Max, went missing last month. During their frantic search for the lost feline, they checked home security footage from the day the cat vanished and saw a neighbor calling the animal over to her. When they followed up on the puzzling scene, they claim that the woman told them she brought Max to her father's farm in a county around 100 miles away and that "he’s having the time of his life." As one might imagine, the revelation prompted a call to the police, who later arrested the neighbor for animal cruelty. However, Max's whereabouts remain sadly unknown.

For more strange and unusual stories from the past week, check out the Coast to Coast AM website.
